A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe the same DMol work. Their full main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-generation experiments, general-graph experiments, ablations and docking outcomes in Tables 1–8 and Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation and docking results and adds baseline comparisons, schedule ablations and motif-distribution measurements, including Tables 9–11.

M1.justification: The core diffusion procedure, loss and selected motifs retain v1's compressed DMol, now called DMol. Section 7 and Appendix G.6 add a proposed scaffold-conditioning procedure: group molecules using RDKit classes or Mol2Vec/Grover embeddings with K-means++, then train DMol separately within groups. This is a limited procedural extension without reported conditioning results.

E1.justification: Both evaluate QM9, MOSES, GUACAMOL, SBM and Planar graphs and retain the same 1PXH/4MQS docking examples. The new schedule and motif analyses use MOSES. Scaffold-conditioned generation is proposed without experimental outcomes establishing additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: DisCo and DeFoG are newly evaluated across the three molecular benchmarks. MOSES loses VAE, JT-VAE and GraphINVENT comparisons; GUACAMOL loses LSTM, NAGVAE and MCTS. Compressed DiGress comparisons also disappear. GruM and the older QM9 baselines remain in v2 Tables 1 and 8, so their rearrangement is not removal.

E3.justification: v2 adds shingle-distance evaluation, a motif-distribution protocol comparing 15 compressed with 15 uncompressed motif categories, and cosine-schedule parameter sweeps against a linear schedule. New comparisons specify 50 sampling steps for DeFoG and report 500 for DisCo. Existing dataset splits, 500 training epochs and principal DMol hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Tables 10–11 add analyses of compression bias through motif frequencies, co-occurrence and node/supernode distributions. Appendix G.5 and Table 9 add schedule-shape and parameter sensitivity tests. Earlier loss, edge-selection and k ablations remain, but the main tables lose explicit compressed/uncompressed DMol and compressed DiGress controls.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added motif-frequency tables provide point estimates without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds DisCo/DeFoG scores, shingle distances, average sampling-step counts, schedule results and motif statistics. Its DMol validity values of 98.3, 87.8 and 86.7 retain v1's CDMol results, rather than demonstrating improvements. Reported compressed-model training times change from 3.0/4.0 days to 60/88 hours, and GruM's QM9 V.U. changes from 85.2 to 85.1.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces a conditional likelihood formulation and claimed ELBO with node/edge-selection decompositions, absent from v1. Appendix F newly defines shingle distance using motif-count vectors. v1's explicit model-equivariance proposition is replaced by a model-invariance statement in v2 Section 3.3; most earlier efficiency and expressivity derivations are retained.

C1.justification: v1's abstract emphasizes validity and speed improvements over DiGress and the additional benefit of compression. v2 makes motif preservation the central platform claim, introduces shingle distance as a contribution, and adds a claimed roughly 4% advantage over DeFoG. Its conclusion broadens biochemical superiority to all reported comparison methods.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning stereochemistry, synthetic feasibility, larger molecular structures and conditional-generation costs in Appendix K. It newly attributes motif-distribution preservation to marginal priors and deterministic perturbation counts, explains schedule sensitivity, and interprets DisCo/DeFoG's higher shingle distances as a novelty versus chemical-quality tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 discloses c = 0.008 as the existing default, supplies scaffold classes and clustering choices for the proposed extension, and revises reported training times. Main hardware, training settings and the code repository remain the same. The default disclosure does not establish a change to earlier experiments.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to flow matching and discrete flow matching, including DeFoG, with substantive discussion of DisCo's sampling tradeoffs. DisCo's underlying work was already cited in v1. New references also support molecular embeddings and criticism of SMILES validity, shifting comparative positioning toward motif preservation and biochemical utility.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and results narrative are substantially revised, and compressed DMol is consolidated under the DMol name. The DiGress comparison moves into Appendix B, efficiency analysis gains a main-text subsection, and the document adds separate motif-analysis, scaffold-generation and conclusion sections plus reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a predominantly single-column layout with wrapped tables. Earlier Figures 1–2 are revised and merged into Figure 1; a new dependency diagram appears as Figure 6. Table 4 gains metric columns, Tables 9–11 are added, and QM9 comparisons are redistributed. Existing motif, molecule and docking images are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: New baseline comparisons, schedule ablations, motif statistics and explicit limitations strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, v2 removes explicit compression controls and introduces a problematic ELBO: Appendix C, Equations 4–7, adds nonnegative KL terms in a claimed log-likelihood lower bound. Its unqualified superiority across all metrics also conflicts with Table 4's shingle-distance rankings. These substantive gains and losses leave the net quality change unclear.
